body.statement: For fixed \(0<\beta_-<\beta_+\le1\), characterize the weakest covariance-aware self-similarity condition under which the procedure generated by \(H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) yields one interval that is uniformly honest over \(\bigcup_{\beta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]}\mathcal M_{T,m}(\beta,L,B,q)\) and has expected length of order \(\rho_{N,T,m}(\beta)\) simultaneously for every \(\beta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]\); also establish impossibility without that condition.
body.justification: Declared smoothness is the central sensitivity input, while unrestricted honest adaptation over a Holder union is unavailable.
body.gap: Classical self-similar bands treat direct or independently noisy curves; they do not characterize self-similarity under nested exhaustion covariance.
body.consumer: Analysts with several plausible smoothness exponents could report one valid interval when the data certify multiscale signal.
